definition: Potentially traumatic events or conditions occurring before the age of 18 (e.g. abuse, neglect, household adversity) associated with poorer health and social outcomes across the life course.
source: Felitti, V. et al. (1998), American Journal of Preventive Medicine; Bellis, M. et al. (2014), Journal of Public Health.

definition: A research and evaluation consultancy; part of the national Changing Futures evaluation team (with Cordis Bright).
source: CFE Research — an independent research and evaluation company (Leicester); part of the national Changing Futures evaluation team with Cordis Bright.

definition: A trained practitioner who has committed, via the Trauma-Informed Champions Charter, to embedding trauma-informed practice within their employing organisation. South Tees identified 67 named champions across 11 services.
source: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures).

definition: The national programme testing system-change approaches for adults facing multiple disadvantage, jointly funded by Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) and The National Lottery Community Fund (TNLCF); £91.8m across fifteen areas of England, 2021–2026. 'Changing Futures' on its own means this national programme; the local delivery is the South Tees Changing Futures Programme.
source: MHCLG (2020) Changing Futures: changing systems to support adults experiencing multiple disadvantage — Prospectus. London: MHCLG.

definition: Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency (RCVDA)'s programme of community-led research, delivered in partnership with Teesside University on behalf of the Health Determinants Research Collaboration South Tees (HDRC ST); the vehicle through which this deep-dive series is produced.
source: RCVDA Community-led Research Programme (ClRP), delivered with Teesside University under the NIHR Health Determinants Research Collaboration (HDRC) South Tees.

definition: A behaviour-change framework (Michie et al. 2011) used in implementation-science analysis of why training does or does not change practice.
source: Michie, S., van Stralen, M. and West, R. (2011) Implementation Science.

full_term: Department of Health and Social Care
definition: The UK government department responsible for health and adult social care policy in England.
source: GOV.UK — Department of Health and Social Care.

full_term: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities
definition: UK government department from 2021-2024, succeeded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). Co-funder with The National Lottery Community Fund of the Changing Futures Programme.
source: GOV.UK — Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (renamed the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government in 2024).

definition: The senior officer each local authority must appoint (jointly with the Secretary of State) to lead its public health functions.
source: National Health Service Act 2006, s.73A

definition: The role that delivers the programme's Enhanced Case Management workstream. Enhanced Case Workers support people who are already in the system, using a multi-agency 'team around the individual' approach, and reach out to people rather than waiting for referrals. It is a higher-intensity role than the Key Worker.
source: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2), Workstream 2 (Enhanced Case Management).

definition: A compilation of discrete implementation strategies (Powell et al. 2015) used in implementation-science literature cited in this report.
source: Powell, B. et al. (2015) Implementation Science (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change).

definition: The statutory regulator for a range of health and care professions in the UK (not doctors or nurses), established as the Health Professions Council by the Health Professions Order 2001 and renamed the HCPC in 2012.
source: Health Professions Order 2001 (SI 2002/254)

full_term: Health Determinants Research Collaboration South Tees
definition: The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR)-funded local Health Determinants Research Collaboration South Tees (HDRC ST) delivered in partnership with Teesside University; the programme within which this deep-dive series (and Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency (RCVDA)'s Community-led Research Programme) is produced.
source: The South Tees Health Determinants Research Collaboration programme website (NIHR-funded).

definition: The function dealing with staffing, employment and people management.
source: Standard management term.

definition: The statutory NHS body that plans and commissions health services for a defined area.
source: Health and Care Act 2022 (ICBs, Part 1)

definition: A measure used to track progress against an objective.
source: Standard performance-management term.

definition: A body responsible for local-government functions in its area; in England, the principal councils established under the Local Government Act 1972.
source: Local Government Act 1972 (principal councils in England)

definition: Cited in the implementation literature as a comparator example of trauma-informed practice in a policing context.
source: Lancashire Violence Reduction Network

full_term: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
definition: The UK government department co-funding Changing Futures. Named MHCLG to 2021, the Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (DLUHC) 2021–2024, and MHCLG again from 9 July 2024.
source: GOV.UK — Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

definition: The programme's cohort: in South Tees, adults in contact with two or more of five intersecting areas of complex need — criminal justice, mental health, homelessness, domestic abuse and substance use (the national Changing Futures cohort, per the MHCLG 2020 Prospectus, is three or more). The series adopts this working cohort definition as its primary frame. Hard Edges 'severe and multiple disadvantage (SMD)' is the foundational prevalence comparator.
source: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2) / MHCLG (2020) Changing Futures Prospectus (working cohort definition); comparator: Bramley et al. (2015) Hard Edges, Lankelly Chase Foundation.

full_term: North East and North Cumbria Integrated Care Board
definition: North East and North Cumbria — the NHS Integrated Care System area covering South Tees. The NENC Integrated Care Board (NENC ICB) is the relevant NHS commissioning body for this geography.
source: Health and Care Act 2022 (integrated care boards, Part 1)

definition: Author of the 2017 (refreshed 2024) Transforming Psychological Trauma Knowledge and Skills Framework.
source: NHS Education for Scotland (2017, refreshed 2024) Transforming Psychological Trauma Knowledge and Skills Framework.

definition: The publicly funded health system, created by the National Health Service Act 1946 (operational 5 July 1948) and now governed by the consolidating National Health Service Act 2006.
source: National Health Service Act 1946 (established the NHS; now consolidated in the NHS Act 2006)

definition: A communication and personal-development approach based on a claimed relationship between neurological processes, language and learned behaviour patterns.
source: ANLP (Association for NLP) — Definition of NLP

definition: The statutory regulator for nurses, midwives and nursing associates in the UK, established by the Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001.
source: Nursing and Midwifery Order 2001 (SI 2002/253)

full_term: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities
definition: The Department of Health and Social Care unit that published the 2022 working definition of trauma-informed practice.

full_term: Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner
definition: The elected office responsible for the governance of policing in a force area — setting the police and crime plan and holding the Chief Constable to account; created by the Police Reform and Social Responsibility Act 2011.
source: Police Reform and Social Responsibility Act 2011

definition: Local shorthand for the Borough of Redcar & Cleveland (and its council).
source: Local shorthand.

full_term: Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency
definition: The publishing host of this deep-dive series.

full_term: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration
definition: The US federal agency (part of the Department of Health and Human Services) whose 2014 report 'Concept of Trauma and Guidance for a Trauma-Informed Approach' underpins much UK trauma-informed practice.
source: SAMHSA (US federal agency, part of Health and Human Services) — Trauma-Informed Approaches; underpinned by SAMHSA (2014) Concept of Trauma and Guidance for a Trauma-Informed Approach

definition: Secondary trauma (secondary traumatic stress) — the trauma symptoms a worker can develop from exposure to the details of another person's traumatic experience; often relatively sudden in onset and closely mirroring post-traumatic stress.
source: Figley, C.R. (1995) Compassion Fatigue: Coping with Secondary Traumatic Stress Disorder.

definition: The designated officer in an organisation responsible for information governance and data risk; referenced in this report in the context of data-sharing arrangements.
source: an information-governance role defined in government data-security policy; not created by a specific statute.

definition: The local delivery of Changing Futures across Middlesbrough and Redcar & Cleveland (population ~278,000), governed by the South Tees Changing Futures Programme Board.
source: STCFP Board Terms of Reference; South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2); later phase: Draft Housing Prospectus (Dec 2024).

definition: The statutory regulator for social workers in England, established under Part 2 of the Children and Social Work Act 2017.
source: Children and Social Work Act 2017, Part 2 (s.36)

definition: A UK membership network and community of practice that builds trauma-informed training, resources and connections across health, mental-health and wellbeing services. Originally NHS-supported, now an independent community interest company (TICA C.I.C.).
source: Trauma Informed Community of Action (TICA C.I.C.)

definition: The named South Tees Changing Futures role responsible for running the Trauma-Informed Practice workstream.
source: South Tees Changing Futures — Trauma-Informed Practice workstream (programme role).

definition: The four developmental phases in the South Tees framework. An organisation is trauma-responsive when Trauma-informed practice (TIP) is the norm and no longer dependent on champions. No South Tees organisation in the evidence base has reached this phase.
source: South Tees Changing Futures programme — the local trauma-informed maturity framework (four developmental phases).

definition: South Tees's local commitment to trauma-informed practice, funded through Changing Futures. It asks every service to recognise the impact of trauma and respond with kindness and compassion, built on six principles: safety; trust and transparency; choice and voice; collaboration; empowerment; and inclusivity.
source: Trauma-Informed Champions Charter (South Tees; funded through Changing Futures).

definition: A whole-system approach to realising the prevalence of trauma, recognising its effects, responding by embedding that knowledge in practice, and resisting re-traumatisation. The series adopts the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) (2022) England working definition, with Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)'s (2014) four assumptions and six principles as the underlying framework.
source: OHID (2022) Working definition of trauma-informed practice (GOV.UK)

full_term: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise
aliases: voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise
definition: The sector Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency (RCVDA) works within and holds the deep-dive work on behalf of.
source: Sector-standard term.

definition: Vicarious trauma (vicarious traumatisation) — the cumulative, gradual transformation in a worker's own inner experience and worldview that results from empathic engagement with trauma survivors over time.
source: McCann, I.L. and Pearlman, L.A. (1990) Vicarious traumatisation: a framework for understanding the psychological effects of working with victims.

definition: Regional bodies established to coordinate approaches to serious violence; the VRU 2021–2023 learning paper on trauma-informed policing is cited in this report.
source: Home Office-funded regional body.

definition: We Are With You (formerly Addaction) — the commissioned substance-use service across Redcar & Cleveland.

One of the strands the programme is organised into. The Delivery Plan sets out six: a governance strand (Programme Management and Ideas Factory) and five delivery strands — Enhanced Case Management, Innovation Fund, Key Worker Support, VCS Infrastructure, and Embedding Trauma-Informed Services. Workstreams are how the programme delivers, as distinct from the five areas of complex need that define who it works with.
source: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2); STCFP Board Terms of Reference.

definition: The operating name since 2019 of the Big Lottery Fund: the UK's largest funder of community activity, distributing money raised for good causes by National Lottery players. Joint funder of Changing Futures with MHCLG.
source: National Lottery Act 2006 (established the Big Lottery Fund, which has operated as The National Lottery Community Fund since 2019).
